title: Derived evaluation of arbitrary left-module sheaves commutes with forgetting scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the common coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $\Lambda$ be any unital ring, and let $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$ be its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use left-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $V:\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C})\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and $v:\Lambda\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}\to\operatorname{Ab}$ for forgetting scalars. For $W\in\mathcal C$ let $\Gamma_W(M)=M(W)$ with its constant $\Lambda$-action. Derived functors are computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; assume the sheaf categories have enough injectives. For every $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C}))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$vR\Gamma_W K\cong R\Gamma_W(VK)\quad\text{in }D^+(\operatorname{Ab}).$$
If $L^\bullet$ is any bounded-below complex of injective module sheaves with $QL\cong K$, then $VL^\bullet$ is termwise $\Gamma_W$-acyclic in abelian sheaves and $L^\bullet(W)$, after forgetting scalars, computes both sides. No injectivity of $VL^m$ is asserted. The comparison is induced by the identity of underived evaluation functors; it is natural in $W$ and $K$. For sites with terminal objects, the comparisons at the terminal objects commute with canonical global-cohomology pullback along geometric morphisms with constant coefficients, whose exact module inverse image is [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. For arrows of objects of one site they commute with the derived evaluation restriction maps. In particular it identifies the underlying abelian group of $H^n(R\Gamma_W K)$ with $H^n(R\Gamma_W(VK))$ for every integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree and its injective-acyclicity proof, extended to bounded-below complexes by derived.tex Tag 05TA, proposition-enough-acyclics (1); canonical comparison induced by evaluation identity

proof.text: Put $A=\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C})$, $A_0=\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, and denote their evaluation functors by $G_W:A\to\Lambda\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$ and $G_{0,W}:A_0\to\operatorname{Ab}$. The functor $V$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1); its hypothesis on sheafification holds on a small site in the common universe. The ordinary module forgetful functor $v$ is exact: kernels and quotient groups carry the induced left action, so forgetting preserves both. Hence $V$ and $v$ act termwise on derived categories, preserve boundedness below and commute with cohomology. There is the literal natural equality $vG_W=G_{0,W}V$, including differentials and restriction maps: both evaluate the same underlying abelian sheaf at $W$. This does not require commutativity or flatness of $\Lambda$.

source.place: 03FD, first paragraph of proof; Modules on Sites 03DA/03DB

proof.text: Let $J$ be an injective left-module sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] with $\mathcal O=\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$ and $M=J$. Its module evaluation takes values in abelian groups, so its higher derived values vanish: the complex consisting of $J$ in degree zero is an injective resolution by [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The comparison therefore gives $H^q(W,VJ)=0$ for every $q>0$ and every $W$. This is exactly $G_{0,W}$-acyclicity of $VJ$. All size and enough-injectives assumptions of the comparison are among the hypotheses here. We have used acyclicity, not injectivity of $VJ$.

source.place: 03FD, second paragraph of proof and objectwise cohomology equality

proof.text: Choose $L$ as in the statement; such a bounded-below injective representative exists by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. By step 1, $VL$ represents $VK$, and by step 2 it is termwise $G_{0,W}$-acyclic. The category $A_0$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applied to the constant integer ring sheaf: abelian sheaves are exactly its module sheaves, since the integer action is forced by addition. Thus clause (3) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] applies to the identity quasi-isomorphism $VL\to VL$. It says that the canonical derived-evaluation unit $Q(G_{0,W}VL)\to RG_{0,W}(QVL)$ induces isomorphisms in every cohomological degree, hence is an isomorphism. On the module side $G_WL=L(W)$ computes $RG_WK$ by the specified injective-resolution convention. After $v$, these two complexes are literally equal by step 1. Composing with the abelian evaluation unit produces the required isomorphism $a_W:vRG_WK\xrightarrow{\sim}RG_{0,W}(VK)$ for every such $L$.

Identify $a_W$ with the canonical right-derived square comparison $R(a)$ attached to $a:G_W\,;v\cong V\,;G_{0,W}$ (the identity in step 1), in the notation of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-cube]. On an injective complex its defining comparison is precisely the abelian evaluation unit used in step 3, because the module evaluation unit already computes $RG_W$. Consequently it is independent of the representative and natural in $K$. To verify objectwise restriction, apply that cube lemma with $B=B'=A$, $B_0=B'_0=A_0$, $G=G_W$, $H=G_{W'}$, $G_0=G_{0,W}$, $H_0=G_{0,W'}$, $P=P_0=\mathrm{id}$, $Q=Q_0=\mathrm{id}$, $U=U'=V$, and output forgetful functors both $v$. Let $e,e_0$ be evaluation restriction along $W'\to W$, and $c,d$ identities. The underived cube equality is equality of the same restriction homomorphism after forgetting scalars, from step 1. The lemma yields exactly $a_{W'}\circ vR(e)=R(e_0)\circ a_W$. Its $R(e),R(e_0)$ are the derived evaluation restriction maps, which proves the stated naturality in $W$.

source.place: 03FD, canonical evaluation comparison; formal derived square lifting as in 0736

proof.text: For a geometric morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, let $P=f^*_{\Lambda}$ and $P_0=f^{-1}_{\operatorname{Ab}}$. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], both are exact and $V_{\mathcal D}P\cong P_0V_{\mathcal C}$ carries the module adjunction unit to the abelian unit. Assume terminal objects and take $G,G_0$ to be global evaluation on $\mathcal C$, and $H,H_0$ global evaluation on $\mathcal D$, with module and abelian outputs respectively. The underived maps $e:G\to H P$ and $e_0:G_0\to H_0P_0$ send a global section to its inverse-image section, via those units. After forgetting, they are the same map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-cube] with $B=\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C})$, $B'=\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D})$, $B_0=\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, $B'_0=\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)$, $U=V_{\mathcal C}$, $U'=V_{\mathcal D}$, output forgetful functors $v$, $Q=Q_0=\mathrm{id}$, $c=\mathrm{id}$, $a,b$ the evaluation identities, and $d$ the preceding inverse-image isomorphism in the direction required by the cube. The unit agreement verifies its underived equality. Its derived equality states precisely that $a_{\mathcal C}$ and $a_{\mathcal D}$ commute with global-cohomology pullback, including the specified exact inverse-image identification. Enough injectives holds for both small sites as assumed; no claim that $P$ preserves injectives is used.

source.place: 03FD and 0736 (lemma-base-change-map-flat-case), derived comparison from adjunction units

proof.text: Finally take $H^n$ of $a_W$ for any integer $n$. Exactness of $v$ proved in step 1 gives $H^n(vL(W))=vH^n(L(W))$: kernels and images are unchanged after forgetting the left action. Step 3 identifies these with the two derived evaluations. Thus the induced isomorphism is exactly the asserted identification of underlying abelian cohomology groups, with all compatibilities already proved in steps 4–5.

source.place: Conclusion from the common evaluation complex

split_report.summary: Retained the arbitrary unital ring statement and existing searches. Proved underlying injective evaluation-acyclicity from the existing ringed-site 03FD comparison, used the existing bounded-below acyclicity criterion for the canonical derived unit, and instantiated the general derived cube twice for restrictions and geometric pullback. No new nodes or claim of underlying injectivity.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the coefficient-forgetting part of det-sf-comparison-affine-continuity proof Steps 2–3, exposed as existing split Step 1; the affine comparison/continuity route is unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Exactness of forgetting module sheaves on an arbitrary small ringed site; needed to form the exact derived lift, not a geometric comparison theorem.
Objectwise 03FD for a single sheaf gives vanishing of underlying abelian cohomology of injective module sheaves.
Generic enough-injectives theorem supplies bounded-below representatives.
Applied to the integer sheaf, supplies the Grothendieck hypothesis required by the existing complex acyclicity criterion.
Its complex clause computes evaluation on a bounded-below acyclic complex; the unit has no more specific replacement for this homological tool.
General exact-square cube compatibility lifts the evaluation restriction and inverse-image unit squares; no geometric route step is replaced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q145-21cb3010a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and every cited node statement. I checked Stacks 03FD (sites-cohomology.tex l.1862, no commutativity used) and 015E (derived.tex l.5717); tags 05TA and 0736 are present. Step 1: forgetful(1) gives V exact; v exact and vG_W=G_{0,W}V are elementary. Step 2: the ringed-site 03FD comparison node (I checked its proof, nothing commutative) plus the one-term injective resolution give H^q(W,VJ)=0, so VJ is acyclic and nowhere claimed injective. Step 3: the dplus representative, Grothendieck at Z_C and leray-acyclicity(3) applied to id_VL give the iso unit; bounded-below injectives are K-injective, so the conventions agree. Step 4: the cube lemma's fac property identifies R(a) with a_W; with P=Q=id, U=U'=V, a..d=id and e,e0 the restrictions, it yields naturality in W. Step 5: the cube with f^*_Λ, f^{-1} and d from lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image; the unit agreement is the underived hypothesis and no claim that P preserves injectives is used. Step 6 is elementary. Small cases: zero ring; point site with F_p (forgotten injective is not injective in Ab but is evaluation-acyclic); M_2(F_p); negative degrees. The étale/commutative nodes etale-module-cohomology-forget, derived-module-underlying-comparison and sbc-injective-module-forget-evaluation-acyclic are special cases, not duplicates. There are no new nodes. I accept the six declared generic tool_uses. Minor, no change: the sheafification-existence hypothesis in step 1 is justified in words with no node cited, as in the reviewed comparison node. The unit binding mismatch for sk-prop-sf-comparison was already there and is left for maintenance.
